ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the cross section of the cylinder is a circle, with center O, and point P is directly above O. The small ball is thrown from point P with an initial velocity v0 horizontally to the right; when the trajectory of the small ball reaches point Q on the right side of the circle, it flies past along the tangent direction of the circle, and the angle between radius OQ and the vertical direction is labeled θ. Reasoning: At point Q, the velocity direction is along the tangent of the cylinder, and the tangent is perpendicular to radius OQ. Since OQ makes an angle θ with the vertical direction, the velocity direction at point Q also makes an angle θ with the horizontal direction. In projectile motion, there is no force in the horizontal direction, and the horizontal component of velocity is always v0, so at point Q there is v_Q cosθ = v0, giving v_Q = v0/cosθ.
